steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Stir sugar and melted butter together in a large bowl. Add eggs and vanilla; mix well. Combine flour, baking soda, and salt; stir into butter mixture until smooth.
Fold in banana slices, sour cream, and walnuts; transfer into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the loaf comes out clean, about 1 hour.
Cool loaf in the pan for 10 minutes before inverting onto a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Janet's Rich Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: This moist banana bread is made with sour cream and sliced bananas to guarantee tender results and a concentrated banana flavor in every bite.

review.reviewBody: With minor variations this is the recipe I've been making for 40 years. It originally came from a home ec teacher and it is beyond awesome. The differences are, first, that I cream the softened butter with the sugar (not melted). I add 1 tsp. lemon juice with the vanilla, and use 1 tsp. each of baking soda and baking powder, and 1-3/4 c. flour. Finally, regardless of how many bananas are used it should equal 1 cup. You will never find a better banana bread, and over the course of 40 years, I've never heard differently. Edited 8/17/09: My original 4/14/08 review should have indicated that I mash the bananas, not slice them.

As other reviewers mentioned, it was very moist and the flavor was good. My only issue was the sight & feel of the bananas in the bread. Slicing them up, instead of mashing or pureeing them, causes them to be quite mushy and purple. I felt like I was biting into a bruise each time I ate a slice. I ended up digging them out before eating in order to salvage the bread. Sorry, but I think I'll stick to mashing or pureeing...but I'll use the rest of this recipe.

This is Martha Stewart's recipe... only Martha's says to use room temp. butter.. and suggests using a mixer for the butter and sugar to make it light and fluffy before adding flour and other ingredients, and a full cup of mashed bananas instead of chopped up like Janet says.. more bananas and mashing them is what many of you said you did to tweak this recipe, and it is better that way. It is a great recipe.

This is quite simply the best banana bread I've ever had. I followed the recipe as stated, with a few additions, to enhance the overall flavor of the bread. 

I added 1/4 tsp cinnamon and 1/8 tsp ground cloves to the batter and 1/2- 3/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips in addition to the walnuts. Almost all the reviewers agree that the bananas should be mashed, so I mashed them. This distributed the banana flavor evenly throughout the dough. 

I also advise against using a mixer for the batter. This would whip too much air into the cake and take away from its dense quality. I baked the bread at 325 and it was perfectly done in an hour and 15 minutes. It cuts easily, thinly and has a great crust. Thank you for a great recipe!

Just want to chime in here and say that this bread is delicious. It came out soft and moist (but not underdone) on the inside with a slightly crunchy exterior. I also left out the nuts with no negative side effects.
....................................
The second time I made it (after writing the review), I didn't have any sour cream, and so I substituted strawberry yogurt. Just thought I'd mention that it is quite tasty that way, too. :o)

With a few slight changes, this was the best banana bread I have ever tasted! First of all, do use room temp real butter and cream it with the sugar. Also, make sure your eggs are room temp. Sift the dry ingredients together and add 1tsp. cinnamon and 1/2tsp. nutmeg. Also make sure you use a full cup of MASHED bananas. With these modifications, you will have the best banana bread on the planet :)
Yhis bread was good right after I baked it. The banana pieces turned brown and were gooey the next day. I think the mashed bananas make a better bread.

Want to take this recipe to the next level?(And even make it gluten free if you want?) Here’s how!: 1. DO NOT melt the butter! Cream together the softened butter and sugar for a few minutes until light, fluffy and whipped-looking. Almost like frosting/whipped cream. 2. Add ROOM TEMP eggs, one at a time. 3. Add sour cream (or vanilla Greek yogurt, which I prefer), mix. 4. Add 2-3 mashed, super ripe bananas. Mix on medium until they’re thoroughly mixed in. Add vanilla, mix again briefly. 5. In separate bowl, mix weighed flour (1.5 cups is 180 grams) (if gluten free, spoon and level 1.5 cups of 1:1 GF flour) baking soda and salt. 6. Add dry ingredients to mixing bowl in 2-3 batches on low, mixing ONLY until combined- mix too much and it’ll be dense and cakes. No one wants dense and cakey! Bake for 40 minutes at 350, then tent foil on top for 20+ minutes until done. Reply with any questions!

I get perfect banana-walnut bread every time with the following changes to the recipe. You need to know how to cream butter and sugar in order to make a shortbread. If you don’t know what that is, look it up and learn how. The banana is the star of the show, so remember that. I like it not too sweet or too buttery because that masks the banana flavor. Also prepare ingredients ahead of time and keep the ingredients chilled just before combining them. Do not use melted butter. (1) Mash up 3 ripe bananas and set aside in the fridge. (2) Stir up 2 eggs and put in the fridge. (3) Sift the flour into a bowl and combine with the baking soda and salt. (4) Chop up 3/4 cup of whole walnuts, removing shell or bad pieces. Don’t make walnut dust. (5) Open up a cup of plain Greek yogurt and set aside. (6) Combine 2 tsp banana extract with 1 tsp vanilla extract and stir it into the banana mash. (7) Cream a half-stick of softened butter with 2/3 cup of white sugar, plus 1/4 cup vegetable oil until almost foamy, about 5 minutes with a hand mixer. (8) In succession, mix in the eggs, then yogurt then banana mash until creamy. (9) Now hand-stir in the flour, 1/3 at a time. Keep it slightly lumpy like pancake batter. (10) Fold in the walnuts and let sit for 5 minutes for the baking soda to activate; otherwise the walnuts will sink to the bottom. (11) Gently fold batter one more time and transfer into a silicone loaf pan, then jiggle it to even out the batter. (12) Bake for 50 minutes, then keep checking every 5 minutes to inspect when it’s done. Know your oven! (13) Cool the loaf. I like to wrap it in aluminum foil and place it in the fridge overnight for the flavors to meld. (14) Enjoy and repeat.

This recipe is really good! But when it cools, it becomes too dense and the outer crust gets too tough. To fix this, I use parchment paper to line the pan and a lighter colored pan. Instead of slicing the bananas, I mash them, but with the original measurements it turns out a little too wet in the middle so I add a couple of tablespoons of flour to the recipe and less banana, and that usually does the trick. I also like to use plain Greek yogurt instead of sour cream for a softer turnout. I add the juice from 1 lemon, 1 tsp cinnamon, a hint of nutmeg, and 1 tsp of salt instead of 1/2 a tsp just because I think it brings out the flavor a bit more. All in all this recipe is very versatile and delicious so I gave it a 4 out of 5 rating. P.S. I use self rising flour as well and that makes it so moist and soft like cake!

Over the years I have made this banana bread recipe many times! We just love the flavor and it is always moist! Today I tried making it as muffins/cupcakes for my grandsons and of course added some chocolate chips to the mix. I also used 1 tsp of baking powder to the mix as someone else had suggested. The muffins cooked in 25-30 minutes and are so moist and delicious. (picture included) In the past I have added some cinnamon sugar on the top of the loaf for a little difference...that too is a a welcome treat in our home. I only once tried slicing the bananas, mashing is my preferred method-I feel it spreads the banana flavor more evenly through the bread. I highly recommend keeping this recipe on hand!
Love this recipe
Great Recipe!! I make it in a 8 in round cake pan and freeze it. When I need a quick dessert, I thaw it and top with a whipped cream cheese frosting. I always get complimented on it. So easy!!
No changes
MAKE THIS ALL YEAR LONG!!!!! THE ONLY RECIPE I USE!
This banana bread was delicious. I added blueberries. My husband liked it so much. I’m on my second batch thank you.

I’ve been making this for years and my family loves it. I double it and make 2 loaves at once (freeze the second loaf so I always have something on hand). I purée the banana, use 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white, add cinnamon and use choc chips instead of nuts. Absolutely delicious and perfect every time
Easy and delicious! I love the banana chunks. I use full-fat plain Greek yogurt instead of sour cream.
perfect recipe.
This is a great and easy recipe. I will keep this in the books and use this from now on. I think next time I will add some chocolate chip chips just to make it a little more special.
